situation.note: separated six months. I see my kids 3 nights a week. I haven't told my parents in Chandigarh because I know what they'll say. the house is so quiet on the nights they're not here that I leave the tv on

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call missing someone you love, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: The quiet house and the fear of your parents become, over seven days, a grief that is allowed to move and a truth that is spoken.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the quiet house and the fear, named without judgement.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the quiet is grief, and the fear of your parents is what keeps it stuck.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the love you feel for your children is yours and cannot be taken.
week_beats.act: You try letting the quiet be quiet, and speaking the true thing to one person you trust.
week_beats.story: A woman who lost her marriage and her daily life with her children shows you what finding footing in the quiet looks like.

understanding.core_struggle: A separated mother who sees her children three nights a week; the house is quiet on the nights they are not there, and she has not told her parents in Chandigarh.
understanding.mirror: You have the children three nights a week, and on the other nights the house is so quiet you leave the TV on.
understanding.insight: You are grieving the life you had while also afraid of the life your parents will call a failure. The TV is the noise you keep between them.

queries.hook: The quiet house on the nights the children are not here, and the fear of what your parents will say about it. I'm grieving someone I loved.
queries.diagnose: Grief is love with nowhere to go, and when it is held back by fear of blame, the mind becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: What is real in us cannot be lost, and what is lost is not us; the love you feel for your children is your own, and it will not be taken from you.
queries.act: Let the grief have its place; speak the true thing to one person you trust; and let the quiet house be quiet for a while.
queries.story: A woman who has lost her marriage and her daily life with her children, who stood in the quiet and found her footing again.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
verse.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
verse.translation: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Arjuna has collapsed on the battlefield and refuses to fight. Krishna asks him what has come over him. Arjuna looks at his own people on the other side and says they would rather die than kill their own kin, so why should he fight. He admits he sees no way to drive away this sorrow that is drying him up, not even an unrivalled kingdom or rule over the gods. He is asking for help from a place of complete helplessness.
verse.for_you: The house is quiet and the grief is drying you up inside, and you are afraid your parents will call this a failure. You are not weak for not knowing what to do. You are asking for help, and that is where clarity begins. Let the quiet be your witness.
verse.try_today: Let the quiet of the empty house be your witness today.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your quiet house and ask for help.
asks: How do I ask for help when I feel like a failure?
Can I feel this grief without it drying me up?
What does it mean to let the quiet be my witness?

verse.speaker: Kausalya
verse.setting: After lashing out at Dasharatha over Ram's exile, Kausalya apologises and explains what grief did to her.
verse.sanskrit: शोको नाशयते धैर्यं शोको नाशयते श्रुतम्। शोको नाशयते सर्वं नास्ति शोकसमो रिपुः॥
verse.line: Grief wears away your steadiness and your judgement. There is no enemy like it.
verse.translation: Grief destroys steadiness, grief destroys learning, grief destroys everything. There is no enemy like grief.
verse.why: Grief makes us wound those we love; apologising quickly heals more than being right.
verse.misuse: Not a ban on grieving; a warning not to let sorrow make your decisions.

prasang.title: Kausalya's reproach and apology
prasang.summary: In her grief Kausalya lashes out at her husband for exiling their son. When he folds his hands and asks her forgiveness, she is horrified, apologises, and explains that grief made her speak.
prasang.story_hook: She said the words; then she saw her husband fold his hands to her.
prasang.lesson: Grief makes us wound those we love; apologising quickly heals more than being right.

verse.meaning: After lashing out at Dasharatha over Ram's exile, Kausalya apologises and explains what grief did to her. She says grief wears away your steadiness and your judgement, and that there is no enemy like it. She warns that sorrow makes us wound those we love, and that apologising quickly heals more than being right.
verse.for_you: The quiet house and the fear of your parents are two sides of the same grief. You see that the silence is sorrow, and the fear of their call is what keeps it stuck. The life you had is gone, and that is a wound. You can let it move.
verse.try_today: Name the quiet as grief, not as a room you failed to fill.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own quiet house, speaking to a parent who has not yet heard the truth.
asks: How does grief wear away my judgement right now?
How do I stop fearing my parents' call?

verse.speaker: Rahim
verse.setting: Rahim on a love so close it needs no news.
verse.sanskrit: जेहिं रहीम तन-मन दियो, कियो हिए बिच भौन। तासों दुख-सुख कहन की, रही बात अब कौन॥
verse.line: The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
verse.translation: Rahim says: to the one who has been given body and mind, who has made a home in the heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling?
verse.meaning: Rahim speaks from a love so close it needs no news. He says that to the one who has made a home in your heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling. He means that the love you hold for your children is already known to them. You do not need to prove it with words or gestures. It is simply there, steady and understood.
verse.for_you: Your children already know the love you carry for them. You do not need to fill the quiet house with noise to show them you are still present. The love is already in the room with you, and it does not need explaining.
verse.try_today: Notice one small moment when your love for your children is already present.
verse.scene_line: You are in a quiet house where the ones you love already know your heart.
asks: How do I trust that they know my love?
Can I let the quiet hold me?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
verse.line: Childhood, youth, old age: the body keeps changing. The wise aren't thrown by the next change.
verse.translation: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes on to another body. The steady person is not bewildered by this.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that just as a person moves from childhood to youth and then to old age, the body passes on to a new one. The wise are not shaken by this passing. The self that truly lives on is never born and never dies. It simply moves from one body to another, just as one changes clothes. Grief comes and goes, but what you are at your core is permanent.
verse.for_you: The love you have for your children is part of your core, and it cannot be taken away. The quiet house at night is a loss, and it is right to feel it.
verse.try_today: When the house is quiet, name one thing you love about your children and hold it in your mind.
verse.scene_line: You are standing in your quiet house, holding the clothes of a life that has passed on.
asks: How do I hold my love for my children when the house is so quiet?
Can I trust my own judgment when grief is so heavy?

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verse.sanskrit: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verse.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
verse.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verse.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

verse.meaning: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion. Rama tells him to sit in a quiet place, let the senses rest, and give undivided attention to one thing. This quiet sitting and steady faith carry a person until understanding becomes natural on its own.
verse.for_you: The quiet house on the nights your children are away is a place where this grief can finally be quiet. Let the room be still, and let your full attention rest on one thing, without trying to fill the space.
verse.try_today: Sit in the quiet house and let the silence be still.
verse.scene_line: You are in your quiet house, and the question is how to cross the sea of confusion.
asks: How can I let the quiet be quiet without filling it?
What is the one thing I can give my full attention to today?
How do I rest in the Self when the house is so empty?

verse.speaker: Yudhishthira
verse.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verse.sanskrit: प्रियवचनवादी किं लभते / विमृशितकार्यकरः किं लभते / बहुमित्रकरः किं लभते / धर्मे रतः किं लभते कथय ॥ प्रियवचनवादी प्रियो भवति / विमृशितकार्यकरोऽधिकं जयति / बहुमित्रकरः सुखं वसति / यश्च धर्मरतः स गतिं लभते
verse.line: Speak kindly and you'll be loved; think before acting and you'll win more; make friends and live happily.
verse.translation: Yaksha: 'What does one gain by speaking kindly? By acting after careful thought? By making many friends? By devotion to what is right?' Yudhishthira: 'One who speaks kindly is loved; one who acts after careful thought wins more; one with many friends lives happily; one devoted to what is right reaches the goal.'
verse.why: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

prasang.title: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.story_hook: Four brothers lay dead by a clear lake, and the voice that killed them was asking Yudhishthira riddles.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

verse.meaning: At a poisoned lake, the Yaksha asks Yudhishthira what brings a person lasting gain. Yudhishthira answers that kindness in speech earns love, careful thought in action brings greater success, many friends lead to happiness, and devotion to what is right leads to the highest goal. The verse proposes that the way you meet the world matters more than the world itself. It asks you to choose a steady mind and to let kindness outweigh any advantage you might gain by being hard.
verse.for_you: You have been trying to win something back in the quiet house, but the Yaksha's answer suggests you are already losing your own steadiness. The life you built is gone, and no amount of careful thought can bring it back. Let the quiet be quiet for a moment.
verse.try_today: Speak one true thing to the person you trust most.
asks: Does speaking kindly mean I must hide my grief?
What is the advantage of being kind when I am so tired?
How do I choose between my own truth and what others expect?

story.title: Sumitra sits with Kausalya
story.story_hook: Two mothers, two sons gone to the same forest, and one of them found the strength to comfort the other.
story.summary: Kausalya weeps for her son gone to the forest. Her co-queen Sumitra, whose own son has gone too, comforts her: he went for a good reason, he is not alone, and you will see him again.
story.lesson: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.

anchor.speaker: Sumitra
anchor.setting: Ram has left for fourteen years; his mother cannot stop weeping, and her co-queen sits with her.
anchor.sanskrit: निवृत्तवनवासं तं द्रष्टासि पुनरागतम्। जहि शोकं च मोहं च देवि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
anchor.line: You will see him again. Let go of this grief.
anchor.translation: You will see him again, back from the forest. Let go of grief and confusion, my queen. I tell you the truth.
anchor.why: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.
anchor.misuse: Comfort for a long separation, not a promise that every loss will be undone.

prasang.story_hook: Two mothers, two sons gone to the same forest, and one of them found the strength to comfort the other.
prasang.lesson: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.

story.hook_title: Both their sons were gone, and Sumitra found the strength to comfort Kausalya
story.teaser: Both their sons were gone, and Sumitra found the strength to comfort Kausalya
story.for_you: Kausalya could only weep because her son was gone, and Sumitra sat with her in that same emptiness. You are in your own quiet house, grieving the life you had while your children are away. The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows.
